identity.title: Tp53/HIF1alpha co-synergistically promotes CRMP4 expression via promoter-proximal interactions in colorectal cancer.

content.abstract: Tumor protein p53 (p53) plays a dual role in cancer under hypoxia, promoting cell cycle arrest and apoptosis, whereas facilitating survival. P53 can either suppress or cooperate with HIF1alpha to regulate hypoxia-driven transcription and metabolic adaptation. However, the precise molecular mechanisms by which p53 modulates hypoxia-induced tumor progression and therapy resistance in colorectal cancer remain unclear. In this study, we report that the expression of collapsin response mediator protein 4 (CRMP4) is highly expressed in CRC cells carrying wild-type p53 under hypoxic conditions and can be compromised by p53 or HIF1alpha knockdown. Wild-type p53 robustly enriches in four binding domains on the CRMP4 promoter. HIF1alpha fails to bind to the CRMP4 promoter in the presence of p53 knockdown. Disruption of the p53 binding region on the CRMP4 promoter or disruption of a key peptide in the formation of p53 tetramers by CRISPR-Cas9 both lead to the destruction of the promoter-proximal interaction, thereby weakening HIF1alpha binding. The positive correlation between this p53-driven DNA promoter-proximal interaction and the expression of CRMP4 is also validated in colorectal adenocarcinoma in vivo. Overall, our findings determine that CRMP4 is up-regulated in CRC cell lines with wild-type p53 upon hypoxia exposure; p53 is necessary for CRMP4 expression, whereas HIF1alpha determines how much CRMP4 is expressed; p53 as a tetramer interacts with four binding domains at the CRMP4 promoter, and facilitates DNA interaction to accommodate HIF1alpha, thereby enhancing CRMP4 expression in a novel epigenetic manner in CRC responding to hypoxia.
